This is the third application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.142/2022 registered at Police Station Rau, District Indore (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 376(3), 376(2)(K) and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 3/4 of the POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 22/02/2022.

2. As per prosecution story, on 18/02/2022, while the minor prosecutrix was doing dusting work,
present applicant forcefully grabber her from behind and shuts her mouth and committed rape upon Bhurelal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133834804/
1 her.

sentences.text: He has also threatened that if she will disclose the incident to anyone, he will kill her brother and sister in law.
Thereafter, prosecutrix lodged and FIR and accordingly, offence has been registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.
Applicant is suffering jail incarceration since 22/02/2022.
Earlier two bail applications of the applicant have been dismissed as withdrawn.
Investigation is over and charge sheet has been filed.
Prosecutrix (PW-5) has been examined before the trial Court and she has turned hostile.
She did not state anything against the present applicant.
Her father (PW-3) and mother (PW-4) also deposed in the same manner and did not state anything against the present applicant in respect of the aforementioned offence.
Applicant is permanent resident of Indore district and final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time.
Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions, as this Court deems fit and proper.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.
5. Learned counsel for the prosecutrix submits that the statement of the prosecutrix has been recorded before the trial Court.

6. Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case diary.
7.

After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix (PW-5) has categorically stated in her statement that present applicant neither threatened nor committed rape upon her; parents of the prosecutrix also supported the statement of the prosecutrix and final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time.

In these circumstances,
I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

8. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.
